## Blast radius update — now FIVE changes, and the count is still rising

Change **2000** ("Order the enrichment queue by soak deadline") took a `Verified -1` today with
optionality as its **only** failing job, at 51s, `LLM-Review +1`. Same signature as the others.

Running total of changes reddened by this gate rather than by their own content:

| change | subject | optionality failure | other failures? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1997 | Resolve access-check client seam at call time | 34s | none — skew was the whole `-1` |
| 1998 | Stop absent-string child oracles failing open | 47s | yes, unrelated and real |
| 1999 | Fail closed on stale KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS rows | 37s | yes, unrelated and real |
| 2000 | Order the enrichment queue by soak deadline | 51s | none — skew was the whole `-1` |
| 2002 | (the fix for this bug) | n/a — branched from current main | n/a |

**Two of the five (1997, 2000) had NO other failure**: the gate was the entire reason for the
`-1`, and each cost its author a diagnosis plus a rebase for a defect that was not theirs.

## The cost is not just the rebase — it is the ambiguity

Both of those authors began by investigating their own code, because a `Verified -1` is supposed
to mean "your change is broken". In one case I compounded it by telling the author to go look
for an eager import that did not exist. The author corrected me: their diff moves an import
*into* a function body — strictly lazier — so it could not have made an optional dependency
mandatory.

That is the real damage. A gate that reds a change for reasons unrelated to the change **trains
reviewers to discount the gate**, and once a `-1` can mean "your base is old", every `-1`
becomes ambiguous. `recheck` discipline exists precisely to keep that from happening — and
recheck does not even help here, since it reruns against the same tree.

## Fix status

Change **2002** (`cd8fdb4622`) is up for review with the guards added, both directions proven:
the guard fires and skips on old-base trees while still running the *other* generator; on
current `main` both generators run and the pytest step collects 4 tests rather than 0; and the
fail paths still fail (injected `assert False` -> exit 1; drifted `docs/cli-reference.md` ->
exit 1 with the staleness message). So the guard cannot make the gate permanently silent.

Until 2002 merges, the remedy for any change carrying this signature is a **rebase onto current
`origin/main`**, not a fix and not a recheck.
